articles.title: When you need more support
articles.summary: In danger right now? Call 000 in Australia or 911 in the United States. Where to turn if you’d like to talk to someone.
articles.keywords: crisis suicide suicidal emergency urgent danger helpline lifeline beyond blue 000 911 988 support help talk someone counselling counsellor therapy therapist eap mental health distress self harm

how: If you or someone else is in danger right now, call 000 in Australia or 911 in the United States.

If you’d like to talk to someone now, open You and tap “Support”. It lists people to talk to in your region, such as Lifeline on 13 11 14 in Australia or 988 (call or text) in the United States, plus any support your organisation has added, like an Employee Assistance Program, under “At work”. The helplines on the Support screen work offline.
nørma supports your wellbeing day to day. It isn’t a crisis service. It doesn’t diagnose or treat anything, it isn’t therapy, and nobody watches what you enter.
steps: If you or someone else is in danger right now, call 000 in Australia or 911 in the United States.
Open the You tab and tap “Support”.
Tap a number to call, such as Lifeline on 13 11 14 or Beyond Blue on 1300 22 4636 in Australia, or 988 in the United States.
Check “At work” for support your organisation offers.
To see the right numbers for where you live, set your region on the Support screen, or under You, in “Preferences”.
know: If something you write in a reflection suggests you may be at risk, nørma shows you contact details for support services. It will not alert your employer or anyone else.
Because nobody monitors nørma, it can’t send help to you. Please reach out directly.
nørma doesn’t replace a doctor, psychologist or counsellor. If you’re finding things hard, speaking to one is a good next step.

articles.title: Download and sign in
articles.summary: Get nørma from the App Store or Google Play and sign in with the email your organisation invited.
articles.keywords: login log in sign in signin password reset forgot invitation invite link expired download install app store google play email account access

how: nørma comes to you through your organisation. When you’re invited, you get an email called “Your space in nørma is ready”. In most organisations you set a password from that email first, using the “Set your password” button. If your organisation uses its own work sign-in, the email tells you there’s no password to set up.

To sign in, you only type the email you were invited on. nørma finds your organisation and opens its sign-in page in your phone’s browser. You enter your password there, or your work account details if your organisation uses single sign-on, and then you’re taken back to the app.
steps: Open the invitation email and tap “Set your password”. Skip this if the email says your organisation uses its own work sign-in.
Install nørma from the App Store or Google Play.
Open nørma, type the email you were invited on under “Sign in to your account” and tap “Continue”.
Sign in on the page that opens, then return to the app.
The first time, read “Before you start” and agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.
know: If you see “We couldn’t find that email”, check that you’re using the exact address your organisation invited. Tap “Get help”: whoever shared nørma with you can check which address was invited.
Forgotten your password? After “Continue”, use “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page. The code goes to the email you were invited on.

The link in the invitation email works once and expires after 72 hours. If it has run out, ask your organisation’s nørma administrator to resend it. Typed your email too many times? Wait a minute and try again.

articles.title: Your first check-in
articles.summary: What to expect from the first twenty questions, and how long they take.
articles.keywords: first check-in start begin onboarding new questions how long relationship single explore

how: After you sign in, three short films introduce your space, the five pillars, and how the check-in, a reflection and the mirror fit together. Then nørma invites you to your first check-in with “Let’s see where you are”.

Your first check-in is the same as every monthly one. Twenty questions across the five pillars (four each), then three about your workplace. Just before the Love & Relationships questions, you answer “One thing first.” (Single or In a relationship) so those questions fit your life. It takes about five minutes, one question at a time.
steps: Watch the introduction films. You can replay them later from You, under “Start again”.
Tap “Start my first check-in”, then “Begin”. Or tap “Explore first” and start your check-in from Home later.
Answer each question with No, Not really, Mostly or Yes. Choosing an answer takes you to the next one.
Just before the Love & Relationships questions, answer “One thing first.” (Single or In a relationship) so those questions fit your life.
Answer the three “Your workplace” questions. Add a private note if you like, then finish.
See your first Fulfilment score straight away, then read your mirror.
know: If your organisation’s check-in isn’t open yet, the button says “Take a look around” and shows when the next one opens. You can explore the rest of the app in the meantime.
You can stop part-way. Your answers are saved as you go, and you carry on from where you left off.

Nobody where you work can read your entries. Your answers and habits reach them only inside group figures, never with your name. Groups smaller than 5 people never show. In a small team, a figure can come from one person.

articles.title: Reminders and notifications
articles.summary: Choose when nørma nudges you, or turn reminders off.
articles.keywords: reminders notifications notify nudges push email alerts pause turn off stop mute gratitude reminder time

how: You decide how often nørma gets in touch. Everything lives under You, in “Preferences”: a reminder when your check-in opens, how often you get nudges, a daily gratitude reminder, and a switch to pause the lot.
Notifications are occasional: your check-in being open, a gentle nudge such as “How are you, really?”, a habit or step you’ve set, or the gratitude reminder.
steps: Open the You tab and tap “Preferences”.
Turn “Remind me when the window opens” on or off for your monthly check-in.
Under “How often can nørma send you nudges?”, choose Daily, Weekly or Off. Check-in reminders still come.
Turn the “Gratitude reminder” on or off. It starts at 20:30 your time. Tap “Remind me at” to change it, then “Save time”.
To stop everything for a while, turn on “Pause everything”.
know: “Pause everything” stops reminders and nudges until you switch it back on. Nothing else changes: your entries and your progress stay as they are.
Your phone’s own settings still apply. If notifications for nørma are off on your phone, you won’t get any, whatever you choose in the app.
nørma emails you the day your organisation’s check-in opens, and the day before if nudges are Daily or Weekly. “Pause everything” stops these emails too.

articles.title: How the monthly check-in works
articles.summary: Once a month: twenty pillar questions, three on work.
articles.keywords: check-in checkin monthly survey questions missed skip window late leader questions answers

how: Once a month, nørma asks the same short set of questions so you can see how things move over time. Twenty questions cover the five pillars, four for each. Three more ask about your workplace: “Do you feel heard?”, “Do you feel valued?” and “Do you feel safe to speak your truth?”.

Every question has four answers: No, Not really, Mostly and Yes. Your organisation sets the window when check-ins open. You can do one check-in each calendar month while it’s open, and if your organisation hasn’t set a window, it’s open all month.
steps: When your check-in is open, Home shows “Start check-in” on check-in day, and “Open now” otherwise.
Tap “Begin”.
Answer each question. Each answer moves you on. You can finish later that month.
Answer the three “Your workplace” questions.
Add a private note under “Anything you want to note from this month?” if you like, then finish.
On your result, tap “Yes, remind me” if asked. Then read your mirror.
know: Missed it? The check-in closes and the next one opens next month. Nothing you’ve already shared is lost. Leaders see how many in a team checked in, never who.

Your pillar answers make your personal score, counted in team figures without your name. The workplace answers sit outside your Fulfilment score. Your organisation sees them only in group figures, never with your name. Groups smaller than 5 people never show. In a small team, a figure can come from one person.
Leaders also get four questions on how they lead. Three feed a leaders’ score seen by leaders at their level and above; the fourth stays private. None of them change your Fulfilment score.
The note at the end is private. Nothing in it is shared with anyone.

articles.title: The five pillars
articles.summary: The five areas of life nørma asks about.
articles.keywords: pillars health fitness internal work love relationships social connection work life flow balance areas

how: nørma looks at five areas of a whole life, called the Five Pillars of Fulfilment. You see them on your Home screen, and the same five appear in your organisation’s results as nameless team averages.

Health & Fitness is how you’re caring for your body and energy. Internal Work is your inner life: mind, attention and self. Love & Relationships is closeness, romance and feeling at peace. Social Connection is friends, community and belonging. Work & Life Flow is how work sits within the rest of your life.
steps: Each check-in asks four questions for each pillar.
Each pillar gets its own score from 0 to 100, based on those four answers.
Home draws your five pillar scores as a shape, and your Fulfilment score is the average of all five.
Habits, growth journeys and growth work are each linked to a pillar, so you can put your energy where it matters to you.
know: Work is one pillar of five. The other four cover the rest of your life, because all of it comes to work with you.
The Love & Relationships questions are worded differently depending on whether you’re single or in a relationship. You can change your answer under You, in “About you”.
Your organisation sees group averages only, never your name. Groups smaller than 5 people never show. In a small team, an average can come from one person.

articles.title: Reading your Fulfilment score
articles.summary: What the number and the shape on Home tell you, and what they don’t.
articles.keywords: score fulfilment fulfillment number shape pentagon result low high about this score history

how: Your Fulfilment score is the average of your five pillar scores, from 0 to 100, with every pillar counting equally. It comes from your monthly check-in answers and nothing else.

On Home, the “Fulfilment” card shows the number in front of a five-sided shape. Each point of the shape is a pillar: the further it reaches out, the higher that pillar scored. The card also shows when your last check-in was and when the next one opens.
steps: Open Home and find the “Fulfilment” card.
Look at the shape to see which pillars are strongest and which are lower.
“About this score”, at the bottom of your check-ins under You, explains how the number is worked out.
To see how it has moved since your first check-in, open You and go to “Your journey”.
Pick your lowest pillar as a starting point in Grow.
know: What you do in the app, like habits and reflections, builds your Momentum. It never changes your Fulfilment score.
The score is a snapshot of how you answered this month. It isn’t a test result, a diagnosis or a judgement, and one lower month is just information.
Your organisation sees group averages only, never your name. Groups smaller than 5 people never show. In a small team, an average can come from one person.

articles.title: The mirror
articles.summary: What you get back after a check-in or reflection.
articles.keywords: mirror feedback result summary ai focus ask again add to it suggestion step

how: After a check-in, your mirror names the pillar to focus on this month, then lets you keep, add or remove habits and growth work for it. This mirror is put together from your answers by fixed rules, without AI.

When you save a reflection, you get a mirror for that too. A third-party AI writes it from what you said and your latest check-in answers. It reflects your words, notes themes and suggests a few small steps. It doesn’t give advice.
steps: Finish your check-in to see your mirror.
Read “Your focus this month” on your result, then your mirror.
Tap “Write today’s reflection” to add your own words, or “Go to home”.
After a reflection, read its mirror. If it couldn’t answer, tap “Ask again”.
You can add to a written reflection later with “Add to it”, and nørma writes a fresh mirror.
know: The mirror is a reflection of what you entered. It isn’t therapy or professional advice, AI can get things wrong, and your own judgement comes first.
Nobody at work can read your mirror. Themes it notes can count towards your team’s themes, never with your words or your name.
If something you write suggests you might be at risk, nørma shows you contact details for support services. See “When you need more support”.

articles.title: Voice and text reflections
articles.summary: Say it or type it. Speech becomes text on your phone.
articles.keywords: reflect reflection journal voice text speak record recording transcription microphone ai privacy

how: Reflect is your space to put a thought down, whenever you like. nørma offers a question to start with, such as “What’s on your mind?”, and you can type your answer or say it out loud.

If you speak, the app turns your speech into text on your phone. If your phone can’t do that on the device, nørma won’t record rather than send your voice somewhere else to be transcribed. In a web browser, transcription also runs inside the browser. Your recording is saved to your account so you can play it back.

When you save, nørma sends your reflection, latest check-in answers, earlier themes and chosen habits to a third-party AI service to write your mirror, pick a small step and note the themes. Your name isn’t sent.
steps: Open the Reflect tab.
The first time, read “A third-party AI reads your reflections” and tap “Continue”, or “Not now”.
Use the question shown, or tap “Another question” for a different one.
Type your reflection, or speak for up to three minutes. You can pause and resume.
Tap “Done” to save, then read your mirror and the themes nørma noticed.
know: Voice recordings have a three-minute limit. The first time you speak, your phone asks for permission to use the microphone and speech recognition.
Your name isn’t sent to the AI. A theme label from your reflection may count for your team and groups above it, never your words or name.
Reflect is for everyday thoughts. If you need to talk to someone now, open You and tap “Support”.

articles.title: Who can see my reflections
articles.summary: Not your employer or manager. An AI writes your mirror.
articles.keywords: who sees reads hears reflections private privacy ai anthropic engineers recording voice employer manager boss data

how: Your employer, your manager and your organisation’s nørma administrators have no way to open your reflections, written or spoken. Recordings are stored encrypted in Australia; the AI may process text overseas. Nobody where you work can play your recordings.

Yes, an AI service reads your reflections. To write your mirror and pick out themes, the text goes to our AI provider, Anthropic, without your name, email or organisation. A small number of named nørma engineers can reach the systems that hold your data, only for operations and support, under access controls. Nobody reads your reflections as a matter of course.
steps: When you save, your reflection and any recording are stored in your account.
The text, without your name, goes to the AI service with your latest check-in answers to write your mirror and note themes.
A theme label, such as a topic you mentioned, may count for your team and groups above it. Your words never go to your organisation.
Your recording is kept in your account so you can play it back. Nobody where you work can play it.
know: The AI gets your reflection as given, plus your latest check-in answers. If you’d rather a name or detail didn’t leave your phone, leave it out.
If you delete your account, your reflections and recordings are erased after 30 days.
Before your first reflection, nørma shows you a short notice about the AI. You can say “Not now” and come back to it.

articles.title: Habits
articles.summary: Small things you do on repeat, each one tied to a pillar.
articles.keywords: habits habit add log streak track routine pillar daily weekly

how: Habits are small things you do on repeat, like a walk at lunch or ten minutes without your phone. Each one is linked to a pillar.

You can pick from habits suggested for you, choose from a list for each pillar, or write your own. Choose how often you’re aiming for, log it on the days you do it, and a 12-week grid shows how it’s going.
steps: Open Grow and tap “Add” by Habits (or “Add your first habit”).
Choose from “Suggested for you” or a pillar list, or tap “Write your own”.
Set “How often”, then tap “Add this habit”. If you write your own, set “How many days a week?”.
Tap “Log today” on the days you do it.
Pause, resume or remove a habit whenever you like.
know: Logging habits builds your Momentum. It never changes your Fulfilment score.

Nobody where you work can see your habit names. Your organisation may see how many habits a group has ticked, never what they are or who ticked them. Groups smaller than 5 people never show. In a small team, a figure can come from one person.
If habit nudges aren’t helping, change how often you get nudges under You, in “Preferences”.

articles.title: Growth journeys
articles.summary: Short illustrated chapters, one pillar at a time, with one thing to try.
articles.keywords: journeys journey chapters foundations deeper into course learning films lessons

how: Growth journeys are short guided chapters, each about one pillar. A chapter takes about five minutes: a short film, a few short reads, one question to think about, and one small step to try.

Everyone starts with “Foundations”. You’ll also see “Deeper into” journeys for each pillar; they aren’t open yet. Your organisation may also add its own chapters, which appear under “From your organisation”.
steps: Open Grow and scroll to the journeys.
Start with Foundations.
Watch the film, read on, and answer the question.
At “One small step”, tap “Take this” or “Skip”.
After Foundations, the “Deeper into” journeys show as “Not open yet” for now.
know: Chapters count towards your Momentum.

Nobody where you work can read your answers. Your organisation may see how many chapters a group has completed, never your words or your name. Groups smaller than 5 people never show. In a small team, a figure can come from one person.
There’s no rush. Take a chapter when it suits you.

articles.title: Reset
articles.summary: Tools for the next few minutes, picked by how you feel right now.
articles.keywords: reset breathing breathe stress stressed anxious anxiety calm sleep focus meditation panic overwhelmed

how: Reset is for the next few minutes, when you need to settle. You choose how you feel right now, and nørma suggests short practices that suit it, from one to twelve minutes, such as “Box breathing” or a “Body scan”.
The feelings to choose from are Stressed, Anxious, Angry, Overwhelmed, Can’t focus, Low and Can’t sleep.
steps: Open Grow and tap Reset.
Choose how you feel right now.
Pick a practice and follow along.
Come back whenever you need it.
know: Reset is a quick tool for everyday moments. It isn’t treatment. If a feeling is overwhelming or won’t ease, talk to someone: open You and tap “Support”.
Finishing a Reset builds your Momentum.
How you’re feeling never leaves your phone.

articles.title: Gratitude
articles.summary: Three small things a day, in about a minute.
articles.keywords: gratitude grateful thankful journal three things daily reminder skip

how: Once a day, nørma asks you to finish the line “Today I’m grateful for…” with three small things. It takes about a minute.
Done most days across a month, it becomes a small habit of noticing what’s going well, alongside whatever else is going on.
steps: Open Grow and tap Gratitude, or tap your gratitude reminder.
Write three small things.
Save them (it ticks “Gratitude Journal”), or tap “Skip today”.
To change or turn off the reminder, open You, then “Preferences”.
know: Nobody where you work can read your gratitude entries, and gratitude is never counted in your organisation’s figures.
The reminder is on by default at 20:30 your time. You can move it or turn it off.
Skipping a day is fine. Come back whenever it suits you.

articles.title: Momentum
articles.summary: What it counts, and why it resets monthly.
articles.keywords: momentum progress points tree character activity streak reset monthly

how: Momentum shows how much you’ve done for yourself this month. Logging habits, writing gratitude or reflections, finishing Resets or chapters, doing growth work and checking in all grow it.

It’s a number from 0 to 100, and nørma, the character on the Momentum card, fills up as it grows. Recent activity counts for more, so it can dip if you’ve been quiet for a while. It starts fresh each calendar month.
steps: Find the Momentum card at the top of Grow.
Tap it to see where you are this month, out of 100.
Open “How momentum is earned” to see what counts.
Do one small thing, like logging a habit or a two-minute Reset, and watch it move.
know: Momentum never changes your Fulfilment score. One shows what you’ve been doing, the other how you answered your check-in.
Momentum is private. It doesn’t appear anywhere your organisation can see.
A fresh start each month is deliberate. A quiet month is fine.

articles.title: What my employer sees
articles.summary: Group figures only, never with your name.
articles.keywords: who sees my answers see answers employer manager boss leader hr company organisation privacy anonymous anonymity confidential private aggregated five minimum names identify

how: Nobody where you work can read your entries. Your answers and habits reach them only inside group figures, never with your name. Those group figures cover check-in answers combined into averages for the five pillars and the three workplace questions, themes that come up across people’s reflections (as labels, never words), and how much a group uses nørma.

Nobody where you work can open your check-in answers, your scores, your reflections, your voice recordings, your habit names or your gratitude entries. Its nørma administrators do see your account details: your name, email, team and role, and whether you’ve accepted your invitation and signed in. They can’t see whether you’ve done a check-in.
steps: You check in. Nobody where you work can read your answers.
nørma combines answers into group averages on its own servers.
If a group has under five people, your organisation sees nothing for it, but its answers count in the group above.
Leaders see the averages for their own group and the groups inside it.
To see this for yourself, open You, tap “Privacy & data”, then “See it the way a leader does”.
know: Groups smaller than 5 people never show. In a small team, a figure can come from one person. The five counts everyone in the group, leader included, rather than how many people answered, so a group of five shows a result from its first check-in. Your organisation can raise the minimum, but never lower it below five.

Using nørma is voluntary, and nørma has no way to make it compulsory. Leaders and administrators don’t get a list of who has or hasn’t checked in. Leaders see how many in a team checked in, never who.

articles.title: Download my data
articles.summary: Download a copy of what you’ve entered, all in one go.
articles.keywords: export download data copy my data json backup gdpr access request

how: You can download a copy of what you’ve entered in nørma whenever you like. The export, called “My nørma data”, includes your reflections, mirrors, check-ins, habits, gratitude entries, Reset days, commitments and settings.
It comes as JSON text, a common format for data that many apps and text editors can open.
steps: Open the You tab.
Tap “Privacy & data”.
Tap “Export everything”.
Your phone’s share sheet opens with your data as JSON text. Save it to your files, or send it somewhere you trust.
know: Voice recordings are listed in the export, but the audio itself isn’t inside it. You can play recordings back in the app while your account is open.
On hold for deletion? You can still tap “Export my data”.
Once your data is on your device, it’s outside nørma, so keep it somewhere safe.

articles.title: Delete my account
articles.summary: Delete from Privacy & data. You have 30 days to change your mind.
articles.keywords: delete erase remove close account deletion leave leaving quit data privacy cancel undo

how: You can delete your account from the app at any time. You don’t need your employer’s permission.
Deleting puts your account on hold for 30 days in case you change your mind. After that, everything you entered is erased: reflections, recordings, check-ins, habits, all of it.
steps: Open the You tab and tap “Privacy & data”.
If you want a copy, tap “Export everything” first.
Tap “Delete account & data”.
At “Delete everything?”, tap “Delete in 30 days”.
Changed your mind? Sign in within the 30 days and tap “Keep my account”.
know: Group figures your answers already went into aren’t recalculated. They never show your name. Records of sign-ins are kept for security, and backups clear on their normal cycle.

If you leave your organisation and it removes you from nørma, you can’t sign in from that day, and your account is erased after 30 days. Meanwhile your administrator can send your data to a personal email you give them, without seeing it. Work addresses are refused, and the link lasts a week at most. If you know you’re leaving, export your data before your last day.
If your organisation restores your access within those 30 days, nothing is lost.

articles.title: Set up your organisation
articles.summary: Departments, teams and who belongs where.
articles.keywords: setup set up organisation structure levels groups departments teams timezone region eap support directory onboarding

how: AOH creates your organisation in nørma. From there, an Organisation Admin builds the structure in “Structure”, which has four parts: Levels, Groups, People and Leaders.

Levels are the names of your ladder, such as Company, Department, Team. Groups are the actual departments and teams, arranged as a tree. A leader assigned to a group sees that group and everything inside it.
steps: In Structure, open Levels and name each level of your organisation.
In Groups, add your departments and teams at the right level.
Add your people (see “Invite your people”), then assign each person to a group under People.
Under Leaders, choose who leads which group and tap “Assign”.
In Settings, set your organisation’s timezone and default helpline region (people can pick their own), and add your own support, such as your EAP, to the Support directory.
In “Group check-in”, set when the monthly check-in opens.
know: Groups are archived rather than deleted, so their history is kept.

Plan group sizes for privacy: a group under your organisation’s minimum (five people, or higher if you’ve raised it) shows no results, and can hide its department’s too. Structure shows each group’s status.
nørma doesn’t replace your EAP. It works earlier, day to day, and sits beside it. Add your EAP in the Support directory (“Add entry”) and it appears in the app under “At work” on the Support screen.

articles.title: Invite your people
articles.summary: Send invites, track enrolment and resend.
articles.keywords: invite invitations enrol enrolment roster csv import resend add people employees users onboarding

how: You can invite people one at a time or import a whole roster from a CSV file. Each person gets an email called “Your space in nørma is ready” with a button to set their password. If your organisation uses single sign-on, the email says there’s no password to set. Leaders and admins get their own version.
Every person on the People page has a status: “Not yet invited”, “Invited”, “Active” or “No access”.
steps: For one person, open People, use “Invite someone”, fill in Email, Name, Role and Team, then tap “Send invitation”.
For many people, use “Import a roster” with the columns externalId, email, displayName, group and role. A group can be a path, such as “EMEA > Sales”. Importing a roster doesn’t email anyone.
Send invitations afterwards: filter to “Not yet invited”, choose “Invite all pending”, and confirm. The button shows the count, such as “Send 12 invitations”.
Watch statuses change from Invited to Active as people accept.
If someone missed it, their row shows “Resend invitation” or “Resend sign-in details”.
know: The invitation link works once and expires after 72 hours. Resend it if it runs out.
A roster import is all or nothing: if any row has a problem, nothing is imported, so fix the row and try again.
Status shows whether someone has accepted and can sign in. It never shows whether they’ve checked in or what they said.

articles.title: Leaders and administrators
articles.summary: Who sees the dashboard, who manages people, and what neither can see.
articles.keywords: roles leaders admins administrators permissions access manager individual answers privacy leader view see

how: There are two dashboard roles. A People Leader sees the results for the group they lead and every group inside it, never above or beside it. An Organisation Admin sees the whole organisation and also manages it: people, structure, participation, the check-in window, privacy settings and integrations. Leaders also see Themes and Alerts. Admins also see Value at Stake, Cohorts and Accelerator.

Leaders and admins are employees too, with their own private app. Neither role can see anyone’s check-in answers, scores or reflections. The People page says so plainly: nørma never shows you an individual’s reflections or check-in answers. Your own check-in counts in your team’s figures, so what you read includes your answers.
steps: Set someone’s role when you invite them, or change it on the People page.
Assign a leader to a group in Structure, under Leaders.
Admins can check a leader’s view: choose “Leader view” and that leader’s group.
If someone asks to see a person’s answers, explain that the dashboard has no screen for them, and neither nørma nor AOH will provide them on request.
know: Admins can see account details on the People page: name, email, team, role and invitation status. That’s there so admins can manage access.
Growth work logs stay yours; leaders above you and admins read your answers to “What have you actioned this month for your team?”.
Please never try to work out who gave a particular answer.

articles.title: Fulfilment and Culture
articles.summary: Fulfilment and Culture for your group, over time.
articles.keywords: fulfilment culture dashboard scores numbers trends themes board export report kpi

how: The dashboard leads with two numbers. Fulfilment is the average of the five pillar scores from people’s monthly check-ins. Culture is the average of three questions: “Do you feel heard?”, “Do you feel valued?” and “Do you feel safe to speak your truth?”.

Beside them sits “Participation this month”, plus a row showing how the group used nørma: active people, reflections, growth work, Foundations chapters and habits ticked. Trends shows the months behind the numbers, six by default. Also see Alerts, which flags groups that need attention, and for admins, Value at Stake, an estimate of what turnover may cost.
steps: Open Dashboard and choose the group you want with the scope switcher.
Read Fulfilment and Culture for this month.
Check the anonymous themes under “What … is saying”, headed with your group’s name.
Open Trends to see the line over time and each pillar. Switch between 3, 6 and 12 months.
To share with a board, use “Export for Board” on Trends and save the page as a PDF.
know: Figures are recalculated once a day, so new check-ins show up within a day.
Each number is an average of the people who answered. When few people answered, it can move a lot from month to month.
Every figure covers a group at or above your organisation’s minimum (five or more people) and never shows individual answers, but a figure can rest on just one answer.

articles.title: Comparing teams
articles.summary: Compare your groups pillar by pillar.
articles.keywords: teams departments compare comparison heatmap pentagon groups table

how: The Teams page compares the groups inside the scope you’re viewing. The Heatmap shows eight numbers per group: Fulfilment, Participation, Culture, Active, Reflections, Habits ticked, Growth work and Foundations.
The Pentagon view, the default, shows each group’s five-pillar shape with its Fulfilment and Culture scores.
steps: Open Teams.
Choose the scope you want to compare inside, such as the whole organisation or one department.
Switch between Pentagon and Heatmap.
Read across the Heatmap to see where a group differs.
Switch your scope to a group to see its own dashboard.
know: A group under your organisation’s minimum (five people, or higher if raised) still appears by name, with “Too few to show.”
A group can also be hidden when showing it would let a smaller group’s result be worked out by subtracting one figure from another.
These are averages. Look for patterns over a few months rather than reacting to one.

articles.title: Focus area
articles.summary: Why one pillar or culture question is named this month, and what to do.
articles.keywords: focus area this month pillar culture lowest priority what to do

how: The “This month’s focus” card names one thing to look at for the scope you’re viewing. It’s either a pillar or one of the three culture questions, with its score.

If any culture question is in the lowest band, the lowest of those is chosen first. Otherwise it’s the group’s lowest pillar. When scores are close together, the card offers it as a suggestion rather than calling it the lowest.
steps: Open Dashboard and choose your scope. Pick a department to see that department’s focus.
Read the focus card and its score.
Tap “Open the session” to see sessions from the library for that area.
Run it with your team, then log the growth work.
Next month, check Signal shift to see what moved.
know: Once check-ins arrive, it names something, even in good months. Treat it as a starting point.
It uses group averages only, which can rest on one answer.
To compare departments side by side, use Teams.

articles.title: Why some groups show nothing
articles.summary: The five-person minimum, and the rule that stops a small group being worked out by subtraction.
articles.keywords: minimum five hidden too few to show privacy anonymous anonymity aggregated suppression small team no numbers

how: nørma only shows results for a group that meets your organisation’s minimum, which is at least five people. Below that, the group shows just “Too few to show.” and no numbers. Your organisation can raise this minimum, but nobody can set it below five.

The five counts everyone in the group, the leader included, rather than how many people answered. A group that’s big enough but where nobody has checked in yet simply waits for check-ins. A group can also be hidden when showing it would let a smaller group’s result be worked out by subtracting one figure from another, for example a department minus all but one of its teams.
steps: nørma counts the people in each group.
If the count is under the minimum, the group’s results are held back on nørma’s servers before anything reaches the dashboard.
If showing a group would let a smaller group be worked out by subtraction, that group is held back too.
Everything else shows as group averages. Organisation Admins can raise the minimum under “Privacy & Safety”.
know: An honest limit: a group of five shows results from its first check-in, so a figure, theme or alert can rest on one answer, yours included. Comparing figures over time can narrow down who might have changed. That’s why we ask everyone never to try to work out who said what.
If a group you need shows nothing, combine it with a neighbouring group in Structure, or read the level above it.
“Privacy & Safety” explains a new minimum; check group sizes in Structure.

articles.title: Growth work
articles.summary: Run a session from the library and log it against the signal.
articles.keywords: growth work actions action plan log share team monthly question status

how: Growth work is what leaders do in response to the signal: a conversation, a session, a change to how the team works. The page shows this month’s question, “Suggested for this scope”, what’s running, programs (admins only), and the library.
Each month nørma asks, “What have you actioned this month for your team?”. Logging growth work against a pillar is what lets you check later, in Signal shift, whether things moved.
steps: Open Growth work.
Choose something from “Suggested for this scope” or The library.
Run it with your team.
Log it: “What signal prompted this?”, “Target pillar”, “What prompted this?” and “Duration (minutes)”. Leaders can also tick “Share this with your team”.
Update its status in the nørma app: Committed, Completed or Skipped.
know: Growth work logs stay yours; leaders above you and admins read your answers to “What have you actioned this month for your team?”. If you tick “Share this with your team”, your team sees the work and its pillar, without your name.
Keep logs and your monthly answer factual and about the team. Don’t name individuals or record what someone said.
Every log is dated, so it becomes part of your evidence trail.

articles.title: Playbooks
articles.summary: What each session is for, who it suits and how long it takes.
articles.keywords: playbooks sessions workshop run team activity library mark as run

how: Playbooks are ready-made sessions you can run with a team. Each card says what the session is for, how many minutes it takes, who it suits, and which pillar and psychosocial safety areas it touches.
Organisation Admins can edit playbooks and deploy them to a team or a program.
steps: Open Playbooks.
Choose a session that fits your focus, your team and the time you have.
Tap “Start session” (on “Session outline” playbooks); “Resume session” continues it.
Afterwards, leaders use “Mark as run” (date, optional note) and answer “What changed for us?”. An admin’s run is recorded automatically.
“Run this next” (top of Playbooks) suggests your team’s next session.
know: Sessions are for the group. Nobody should be asked to share their check-in answers or reflections.
Sessions support good team practice. They aren’t therapy or clinical care.
Marking a session as run logs it against the month, so you can read it against next month’s numbers.
Your note and your answer to “What changed for us?” are private to you.

articles.title: Did it move?
articles.summary: Reading next month’s numbers against what you did.
articles.keywords: did it move signal shift impact results change effect measure before after

how: Signal shift, under Measure, puts what you did next to what happened. Each action you logged yourself sits beside the movement in its pillar since that month, and recorded sessions show a before and after. Other leaders’ logs don’t appear.
nørma shows movement and doesn’t claim your action caused it. Other things change in a month too.
steps: Log your growth work or session in the month you do it.
Wait for the next check-in. Figures update daily as people answer.
Open Signal shift.
Read each action next to its pillar’s movement.
Decide whether to keep going, change approach, or try the next session.
know: Movement isn’t proof of cause.
Small groups and low participation make numbers swing. Look at Trends over a few months before drawing conclusions.
Results only show for groups that meet your organisation’s minimum group size.

articles.title: Check-in schedule
articles.summary: When check-ins open and close, and when the signal arrives.
articles.keywords: schedule check-in window open close dates timing reminders emails calendar

how: An Organisation Admin sets one check-in window for the whole organisation in “Group check-in”. You choose the day (for example the first Monday of the month, or a date), a time, and how long it stays open, from 15 to 89,280 minutes (62 days). It runs in your organisation’s timezone.

Each person can do one check-in per calendar month, and can only start it while the window is open. If you don’t set a window, people can check in any time during the month. nørma emails anyone with reminders on, the day before and the day, and sends a push notification when it opens to everyone who hasn’t turned that reminder off. Group figures are recalculated daily, so results build up as people answer.
steps: Open “Group check-in”.
Choose the check-in day and time.
Set the duration.
Save it.
Let people know, and consider booking a regular slot in the calendar for it.
know: A short window is easy to miss. Give people a few days so it fits around their work.
Results update once a day, so a check-in appears in the dashboard within a day.
Groups below your organisation’s minimum number of people show nothing, however many check in.

articles.title: Raising participation
articles.summary: What helps people take part, and what to avoid.
articles.keywords: participation response rate completion low engagement mandatory compulsory voluntary reminders who checked in

how: The Participation page, for Organisation Admins, shows this month’s check-in completion, overall and for each group that meets your organisation’s minimum group size. The Activation and Active people tiles say “Not measured yet” for now. “Groups needing support” lists teams under 50%.
It never lists who has or hasn’t checked in. Participation is a group figure only.
steps: Open Participation.
Look at “Groups needing support”.
Talk with the leader of that group about what would help.
Make time for it: a regular monthly slot in the calendar makes checking in normal.
Show people what you did with the last results: tick “Share this with your team” when you log growth work.
know: Using nørma is voluntary, and nørma has no way to make it compulsory.
Avoid asking individuals whether they’ve checked in, and never link it to performance. People take part when they trust it’s private and see something change.
nørma sends check-in reminders automatically. The “Send Reminder” button on this page doesn’t send anything yet.

articles.title: Work Check
articles.summary: Coming soon: a planned quarterly check, mapped to WHS psychosocial hazards.
articles.keywords: work check whs psychosocial hazards alerts compliance risk safety

how: Work Check isn’t switched on in the dashboard yet. We’ll update this article when it is.
Work Check and hazard mapping aren’t available in the dashboard yet. For now, Alerts shows where a group’s signal needs attention, and you can record your response as growth work.
steps: Open Alerts to see which groups need attention.
Record what you do about it as growth work, so you have a dated record.
For your WHS records, use “Export for Board” on Trends and save the page as a PDF. A hazard register export isn’t available yet.
know: These insights support your organisation’s WHS processes and professional consultation. They don’t replace them.
Alerts follow your organisation’s minimum group size and never name anyone, but an alert can rest on one answer.
To ask about Work Check, contact your nørma contact.

articles.title: Your evidence trail
articles.summary: A dated record of what you identified, did and reviewed.
articles.keywords: evidence regulator iso 45003 audit export whs records compliance board report

how: As you use nørma, it keeps a dated record: monthly group figures over time, every growth work log (with the scope and when it was logged), and sessions marked as run.

Together, that shows you identified risks, acted on them and reviewed what happened. It’s evidence of reasonable steps. It doesn’t make you compliant on its own, and it isn’t legal advice, so confirm the specifics with your own advisers.
steps: Log growth work and sessions as you go, so the record builds itself.
On Trends, use “Export for Board” and save the page as a PDF.
Keep it with your WHS records, and review it each quarter.
know: Figures are aggregated but can reflect one answer; growth work logs record their author.
There isn’t yet a single one-click evidence pack, and a hazard register export isn’t available yet. Today, “Export for Board” on Trends is the one export.
nørma supports your psychosocial risk management. It doesn’t replace consultation with workers or your duty to put controls in place.

articles.title: People and structure
articles.summary: Move people between teams and handle leavers.
articles.keywords: people structure move transfer team leavers leaver offboarding remove access restore data copy

how: You can move someone to another group in Structure, under People. (In the newer console, change it on their row.) Past months’ figures don’t change; this month’s follow the new team.

When someone leaves, use “Remove access”. They’re signed out everywhere, can’t sign in again, stop counting in your figures from that day, and their account is erased after 30 days. If you restore their access before then, nothing is lost.
steps: To move someone, open Structure and change their group under People.
For a leaver, open People, choose “Remove access” and confirm.
After removing access, offer “Send them a copy of their data” and type their personal email.
If it was a mistake, choose “Restore access” within 30 days.
know: The data copy goes straight to the person. You only ever see a masked address, never their data. Addresses on your organisation’s domain are refused. The link lasts up to 7 days; you can send it three times, and each send replaces the last.
Removing people can take a group below your organisation’s minimum, and then its results stop showing.
Groups are archived, never deleted, so history is kept.

articles.title: Sign-in and SSO
articles.summary: Single sign-on, set up by AOH.
articles.keywords: sso single sign-on saml openid oidc okta azure entra login sign in password identity provider it integration

how: People can sign in with a password they set from their invitation, or with your organisation’s own work accounts through single sign-on (SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect). Either way, they type their work email and nørma sends them to the right sign-in page.

Single sign-on is set up by AOH. There are no SSO settings in the dashboard; ignore the “Okta SSO” placeholder on the Integrations page. Once AOH connects single sign-on, everyone is sent to your organisation’s sign-in page, so agree a switch-over time first.
steps: Ask your nørma contact to set up single sign-on.
Your IT team provides your identity provider’s details for SAML or OpenID Connect.
Agree a switch-over time, then AOH connects it. Test it with one person straight away.
New invitations then tell people there’s no password to set.
know: You don’t need an IT integration to use nørma. It runs on its own: you add people by invitation or CSV import, and single sign-on is optional.
Connections to HR systems and other tools are listed on the Integrations page. Most show “Not built yet”, so a CSV import is the way to load your roster for now.
When someone leaves, also use “Remove access” on the People page.

articles.title: Seats and billing
articles.summary: Billing is in your agreement.
articles.keywords: billing seats licences licenses enrolment pricing price invoice cost payment contract

how: There’s no billing or seat screen in the dashboard. How enrolment is counted and billed is set out in your organisation’s agreement with AOH.
The People page shows who is on your roster and each person’s status: not yet invited, invited, active or no access.
steps: Open People to see who is on your roster.
Filter by status to see who has been invited and who is active.
Use “Remove access” for leavers so your roster stays current.
For billing questions, contact your nørma contact.
know: Employees never pay for nørma and are never asked for payment in the app.
Roster status shows access only. It never shows how anyone uses the app or what they entered.
